text:
사람은 자기가 *믿고 싶은* 걸
믿는 존재라는 걸 알아야 돼요
en: You have to know: people believe what they want to believe.
Facts alone don't make people believe.
After the 9/11 attacks,
a group in Britain
claimed 9/11 was staged by America.
People who believed that conspiracy
started to appear.

text:
그래서 *BBC* 방송국에서
그 사람들 몇 명을 데리고
en: So the BBC took a few of them
and followed them on camera.

text:
그래서 그 사람들의 의혹을
하나하나씩 객관적인 진리를
en: It was a program that took their doubts one by one
and answered each with the facts.
One of them was Charlie Veitch.

text:
그리고 막 그런
객관적인 설명을 하면서
en: As the facts were laid out,
Charlie began to change his mind.
Then he met the victims' families
and realized he had been wrong.
But here's the problem.
Back at the hotel, Charlie

text:
강렬한 깨달음을 한 것이
*자기 혼자*뿐임을 알고
en: found he was the only one who'd seen it,
and it shocked him.
The others believed the families
had been brainwashed by the FBI
or were actors hired by the BBC.
He said it publicly:
"I believed the conspiracy, but the facts

text:
내가 잘못된 것을 깨달았다"고
방송을 하자마자
en: showed me I was wrong." The moment it aired,
a flood of conspiracy theorists attacked him,
sent those emails to his daughter,
and cursed his wife.
So he changed his identity and his name,
and that's how he lives in Britain today.

text:
당신은 당신이 생각한 것보다
*똑똑하지* 않다라는 거예요
en: You're not as smart as you think.
We live sure of ourselves.
So we fight.
When our opinion meets resistance, we get angry.
Because we never think we're wrong,
life fills with conflict.
